Section 3.21 ELT Extract, Load, Transform: load raw data first, then transform in the target. Raw sensitive data lands unmasked. Section 3.23 ETL Extract, Transform, Load: copy data out of sources, reshape and clean it, write it to a target. Section 3.16 Extract Reading data out of a source system without changing it. Section 3.19 Full extract / incremental extract Reading everything every time, versus only what is new or changed since last time. Section 3.19 Integration (ETL) engine The program that actually reads, transforms and writes rows. Section 3.24 Load Writing transformed rows into the target correctly, repeatably and fast enough. Section 3.22 Lookup (ETL) Enriching a row by finding a related value in a reference table. Section 3.21 Mapping (ETL) The definition of how source columns become target columns; also, narrowly, translating codes like S to Shipped. Section 3.21 Mapplet (ETL) Informatica's reusable group of transformations, built once and used in many mappings. Section 3.26 Metadata repository (ETL) A database storing mapping and connection definitions and run history. Section 3.24 Operational database (OLTP) The database an application uses to run the business, built for many small fast reads and writes. Section 3.17 Reconciliation Comparing counts and totals between two stages to show nothing was lost or invented. Section 3.28 Reject (error) row A row the job could not process, written aside with a reason instead of stopping the run. Section 3.27 Scheduler Starts jobs at the right time or after another job finishes. Section 3.24 Session (ETL) A runnable instance of one mapping with its run settings. Section 3.25 Slowly changing dimension (SCD) A way to keep history in a warehouse table when descriptive data, like an address, changes. Section 3.22 Staging area A temporary landing zone where extracted data sits unchanged before transformation. Section 3.20 Streaming Processing each event within seconds of arrival. Section 3.23 Transform Turning staged raw data into the clean, correctly typed shape the target needs. Section 3.21 Transformation One operation on rows, such as filter, lookup or aggregate. Section 3.25 Truncate and load A full refresh: empty the target table, then insert everything. Section 3.22 Type conversion Turning text into real dates and numbers so sorting and arithmetic work. Section 3.21 Upsert "Update if the row exists, insert if it does not." Section 3.22 Watermark A saved marker, such as the last order id loaded, telling the next run where to start. Section 3.19 Workflow / job (ETL) A set of sessions and steps with an order and conditions, started by a schedule or trigger. Section 3.25

Section 4.32 Conditional constraint (Informatica) A table-level rule limiting one column by another, such as To_City not equal to From_City. Section 5.23 Conformance (Informatica) The percentage of rows that fit a rule or pattern; a threshold lets a few disagree. Section 4.25 Connection (Informatica) Saved access to a database, repository or service; plans choose source, target, staging, lookup and storage connections. Section 4.10 Criteria parameter (Informatica) A named placeholder in an entity filter so the value can change at run time. Section 4.25 Custom rule (Informatica) A global rule that uses the logic of an imported PowerCenter mapplet. Section 4.31 Data generation (Informatica) Creating new realistic but fictional rows from rules instead of copying real ones. Section 5.15 Data Integration Service (Informatica) The application service that performs discovery profiles and data coverage tasks. Section 4.4 Data integrity for subset (Informatica) A plan setting for how far subsetting follows relationships: Transactional (default), Referential Only, One-way or Two-way. Section 5.29 Data pattern and metadata pattern (Informatica) Two regular expressions on a data domain: one matches values, the other matches column names. Section 4.22 Data set (Informatica) A named collection of tables in the test data warehouse; storing it again creates a new version. Section 5.44 Data Validation Option (Informatica) A separate Informatica solution used with PowerCenter to check that target data is accurate. Section 4.39 Effective Dates technique (Informatica) Fills start and end date columns so periods follow one another without overlap. Section 5.22 Encryption masking (Informatica) Standard (AES, CRC, MD5) or format-preserving encryption; the latter can be decrypted with the same pass phrase. Section 5.6 Entity (Informatica) A driving table plus all tables related to it by constraints; the unit copied to a subset. Section 4.42 Entity profile (Informatica) A profile that finds possible entities by comparing column names across source tables. Section 4.30 Exception handling (Informatica) Per-rule settings for nulls, blanks and errors, plus optional pre- and post-processing expressions. Section 5.5 Exception test data (Informatica) Deliberate nulls and invalid values, set as percentages, mixed into generated output. Section 5.21 Expression Builder (Informatica) A dialog for building a formula by picking functions and columns. Section 6.4 Offline certificate (GenRocket) A file letting the runtime run scenarios without internet; organisation-specific and valid 24 hours. Section 6.6 Organization resource (GenRocket) A named folder setting, such as resource.output.directory, each user fills with their own path. Section 6.23 Output format (GenRocket) The shape of the result: delimited, fixed-width, JSON, XML, Excel, SQL statements and many more. Section 6.22 Parent, child and sibling domains (GenRocket) A child has exactly one parent whose key it uses; a "describing" lookup table is marked a sibling. Section 6.15 PermutationGen (GenRocket) Generates all possible combinations of the values it is given. Section 7.6 Preview (GenRocket) Sample generated values shown in the web platform so you can check before downloading. x: 10.29 Delphix Algorithm (Delphix) The recipe that replaces a real value with a safe one. Profiling only chooses it; the masking job runs it. Section 8.40 Algorithm framework (Delphix) A kind of algorithm you configure into instances, such as Secure Lookup or Segment Mapping. Section 9.1 Algorithm instance (Delphix) A named framework plus settings, such as dlpx-core:FirstName. This is what you assign to a column. Section 9.1 Algorithm key (Delphix) A secret value inside most algorithms; changing it changes every output. Section 9.1 Algorithm syncability (Delphix) Copying algorithms between engines so both mask alike. Non-deterministic ones cannot be synced. Section 8.36 Application (Delphix) A tag naming the system whose data you manage; create one before an environment. Section 8.17 ASDD profiler (Delphix) Automated Sensitive Data Discovery, the current profiler, using classifiers instead of the legacy search expressions. Section 8.40 ASDD Standard (Delphix) The recommended built-in profile set, with path, type, regex and list classifiers. Section 8.44 Assignment threshold (Delphix) The minimum confidence before the profiler writes a domain and algorithm into the inventory. Section 8.40 Async Task (Delphix) A background task whose ID you can search under Monitor, Async Tasks. Section 8.4 Character Mapping (Delphix) A keyed one-to-one swap of characters within groups you define; unlisted characters stay. Suits key columns. Section 9.4 Checklist (Delphix) An action checking that every table in a rule set has a primary key, an indexed identity column or a logical key. Section 8.35 Classifier (Delphix) One recognition rule tied to one domain, such as a column name that looks like ssn. Section 8.40 Classifier framework (Delphix) A kind of classifier: PATH (table and column name), TYPE (data type and length), REGEX (data) or LIST (values in a list). Section 2.7 Collision (Delphix) Two different real values masked to the same fake value. Section 8.7 Confidence (Delphix) A 0 to 100 score for how sure the profiler is about a match. Section 8.40 Connector (Delphix) Saved details the engine uses to reach one database or set of files. Section 8.18 Containerized engine (Delphix) The engine run as a Kubernetes pod of three containers; meant for ephemeral use, and without FTP file masking. Section 8.8 Continuous Compliance engine (Delphix) The product that discovers sensitive data and masks it; also called the masking engine or Compliance Engine. Section 8.1 Continuous Data engine (Delphix) The virtualization product that creates VDBs; never run it in the same machine as the masking engine. Section 8.24 Copybook (Delphix) A rule set type for mainframe data sets described by a copybook. Section 8.31 Date Shift (Delphix) Moves a date within a range, never back onto itself. Fixed shifts are deterministic; variable ones are not syncable. Section 9.9 Dependent Date Shift (Delphix) Masks two related dates together, keeping their order and interval. Section 9.4 Domain (Delphix) A named kind of sensitive data, such as FIRST_NAME, with exactly one default masking algorithm. Section 8.1 dSource (Delphix) The engine's compressed copy of a source database from which VDBs are made. Section 8.24 Encoding (Delphix) How characters become bytes. ASCII and UTF-8 for most file types; mainframe data must be EBCDIC. Section 9.17 End-of-record (Delphix) The characters ending a line: LF on Linux, CR+LF on Windows. Section 9.15 Environment (Delphix) A folder-like container inside an application holding connectors, rule sets and jobs. Its purpose is Mask or Tokenize/Re-Identify. Section 8.17 Extended connector (Delphix) A connector on an uploaded JDBC driver, for databases not supported natively. Section 8.16 File connector and file rule set (Delphix) The connector says where files are; the rule set lists which files or name patterns and which format each uses. Section 9.15 File format (Delphix) A small uploaded description of a file's field names (and lengths for fixed width). Metadata only. Section 9.19 Free Text Redaction (Delphix) Blanks sensitive words and patterns inside notes columns; needs expertise to configure. Section 2.32 Identity column (Delphix) A column that numbers rows automatically; the engine can use one as the key or add a temporary one. Section 8.28 In-place / on-the-fly (Delphix) In-place changes data where it sits; on-the-fly reads a source and writes masked data to a target. Section 9.11 Inventory (Delphix) The table of every column or field in a rule set with its domain and algorithm: profiler output, masking input. Section 8.40 JDBC (Delphix) Java Database Connectivity. The engine uses a JDBC driver per database and a JDBC URL to say where to connect. Section 8.16 Job (Delphix) A saved runnable task: profiling, masking, tokenization or re-identification.
